title: Payment API returning HTTP 500
symptoms: payment api 500 error, internal server error, transactions failing, payment request fails, payment service error, checkout failing
checks: Check application logs for stack traces around the failure time
Check if the database is reachable and the connection pool is not exhausted
Check downstream dependencies such as the bank gateway or auth service
Check if a deployment or config change happened recently
resolution: If a recent deployment caused it, roll back. If the DB pool is exhausted, fix leaked connections and restart the service. If a downstream service is down, enable fallback and escalate to that team.
team: L2 Application Support, then L3 Technical Engineering

title: Database connection pool exhausted
symptoms: too many connections, connection timeout, cannot get connection from pool, database connection failures, db connection errors, application hangs on database calls
checks: Check active vs max connections on the database
Look for long running or blocked queries
Check the application for connections that are not being closed
Check for a sudden traffic spike
resolution: Kill blocked sessions, tune the pool size, and fix connection leaks in code then redeploy.
team: L3 Technical Engineering and DBA team

title: High API latency or timeouts
symptoms: api slow, response time high, request timeout, gateway timeout 504, latency spike, pages loading slowly, slow response
checks: Check the APM dashboard for slow endpoints
Check CPU and memory on application servers
Check database query times
Check network latency between services
resolution: Scale out the service, optimise the slow query, or increase the timeout only as a temporary measure.
team: L2 Application Support, Infrastructure Operations if resource related

title: Disk space full on server
symptoms: no space left on device, disk full, log files huge, service crashed writing to disk, disk usage 100 percent, storage alert
checks: Run df on the server to find the full mount
Find large files with du on that mount
Check that log rotation is working
Check for core dumps or temp file buildup
resolution: Archive or delete old logs, fix log rotation, and extend the volume if needed.

title: SSL certificate expired
symptoms: certificate expired, ssl error, https not working, handshake failure, certificate verify failed, browser shows not secure warning
checks: Check the certificate expiry date with openssl
Check which service or load balancer holds the certificate
Check if the auto renewal job failed
resolution: Renew and install the certificate, restart or reload the service, and fix the renewal automation.

title: Failed deployment or release
symptoms: deployment failed, pipeline failed, release broke application, build failed, service not starting after release, ci cd failure
checks: Check the CI/CD pipeline logs for the failing stage
Check application startup logs
Compare config and environment variables with the last good release
Check dependency or version mismatches
resolution: Roll back to the last good release, fix the failing stage, then redeploy.

title: High CPU usage on server
symptoms: cpu 100 percent, high cpu usage, server very slow, cpu alert, load average high, process consuming cpu
checks: Identify the top process using CPU with top
Check if a runaway job, loop or batch process is running
Check for a traffic spike on the monitoring dashboard
Check if a recent release changed behaviour
resolution: Stop or restart the runaway process, scale out if load is genuine, and raise a ticket for the code fix if a release caused it.
team: Infrastructure Operations, then L3 Technical Engineering

title: Memory leak or out of memory errors
symptoms: out of memory, oom killed, memory usage keeps growing, java heap space error, service restarts randomly, memory alert
checks: Check memory trend on the monitoring dashboard
Check system logs for OOM killer messages
Check application heap settings and recent code changes
Check if restarts line up with memory hitting the limit
resolution: Restart the service to restore availability, increase memory limits as a temporary step, and raise a problem ticket for developers to find the leak.

title: Authentication or login failures
symptoms: 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, login failed, users cannot sign in, invalid token, token expired, authentication error
checks: Check the auth service health and logs
Check if tokens or API keys have expired
Check clock sync between services
Check for recent changes to permissions, secrets or identity provider settings
resolution: Renew expired tokens or secrets, fix the permission change, and restart the auth service if it is unhealthy.
team: L2 Application Support and Security team

title: Message queue backlog
symptoms: queue backlog, messages piling up, consumer lag, events not processed, queue depth high, delayed processing, kafka lag
checks: Check queue depth and consumer lag on the dashboard
Check if consumers are running and healthy
Check consumer logs for repeated errors or poison messages
Check if the downstream system is slow
resolution: Restart or scale consumers, move poison messages to a dead letter queue, and fix the downstream slowness.
team: L2 Application Support, then L3 Technical Engineering

title: DNS or network connectivity issue
symptoms: cannot reach service, connection refused, host not found, dns resolution failed, network unreachable, packet loss, connection reset
checks: Ping the target and check DNS resolution with nslookup
Check firewall and security group rules
Check if the target service is listening on the expected port
Check for recent network or DNS changes
resolution: Fix the DNS record or firewall rule, and restore the service port. Escalate to the network team if the problem is between sites.

title: Bank or third party gateway unavailable
symptoms: bank gateway down, third party api not responding, upstream service unavailable, 502 bad gateway, 503 service unavailable, partner api failing, payment gateway timeout
checks: Check the third party status page or partner contact channel
Check connectivity and certificates to the partner endpoint
Check error rates by partner on the dashboard
Check if the circuit breaker or retry logic has kicked in
resolution: Enable the fallback or retry path where available, inform the business of customer impact, and escalate to the partner using the agreed contact process.
team: L2 Application Support and Partner Integration team

title: Transaction reconciliation or settlement mismatch
symptoms: reconciliation mismatch, settlement file missing, transaction count does not match, duplicate transactions, missing transactions, settlement delayed
checks: Compare transaction counts between the application and the settlement file
Check if the batch or file generation job ran successfully
Check for failed or stuck transactions in the database
Check for duplicate processing caused by retries
resolution: Rerun the failed batch job, correct the stuck records through the approved process, and share the mismatch report with the business team.
team: L2 Application Support and Finance Operations

title: Pod or container crash loop
symptoms: crashloopbackoff, pod restarting, container keeps restarting, kubernetes pod not ready, imagepullbackoff, container exited
checks: Check pod status with kubectl get pods
Check pod logs and previous container logs
Check events with kubectl describe pod
Check resource limits, image name and config or secret references
resolution: Fix the config, image or resource limit causing the crash, then redeploy. Roll back the release if it started after a deployment.

title: Backup job failed
symptoms: backup failed, backup job error, backup not completed, restore point missing, backup storage full, scheduled backup missed
checks: Check the backup job logs for the error message
Check free space on the backup target
Check credentials and network access to the backup location
Check the last successful backup time
resolution: Fix the cause, rerun the backup manually, and confirm that it completes. Report any gap in backup coverage.
